proofs.text: Read the host off each of five remote URLs and verify `https://github.com/acme/demo.git` and `git@github.com:acme/demo.git` give `github`, the two Azure DevOps URLs give `azure` and an unknown host gives nothing; verify a project with no remote reads no host. Then run `--gate recorded` on a GitHub remote and verify the config reads `github` with the workflow written, on an Azure remote and verify `purlin.azure-pipelines.yml` with `Azure DevOps` in the output, and on a GitHub remote with `--ci ado` and verify the pipeline file and `azure` in the config

reasons: PROOF-14 happy_path_only: No proof of this rule names a rejection, an error or a boundary.
rule_text: The git host is read from the remote URL as `github`, `azure` or nothing at all, and `--ci` overrides what the remote said

tests.body:
def test_the_host_is_read_from_the_remote(self):
        made = Project('pytest', remote='https://github.com/acme/demo.git')
        try:
            made.run('--gate', 'recorded')
            assert made.config()['ci'] == 'github'
            assert made.has('.github/workflows/purlin.yml')
        finally:
            made.close()
tests.name: test_an_azure_remote_gets_the_pipeline
